title: Privacy policy — Niko
doc.title: Privacy policy
doc.intro: Niko stores only what it needs to run its Discord features, keeps it for no longer than the feature or the law requires, and never sells it. This page is the public, human-readable version of the policy, including Niko's full data retention schedule.
s0.title: Who we are
s0.body: Niko is a free, volunteer-run Discord bot. It is not a company, a registered business, a partnership, or any other legal entity: it is built and maintained by individuals in their personal capacity, in their own time. In this policy, “we”, “us” and “Niko” mean those maintainers, and “official instances” means the Niko bot and the website we operate ourselves at https://niko.sryze.cc, together with its dashboard, public leaderboards, support server, and web forms.
s1.title: Which instances this policy covers
s1.body:
This policy describes how the official public Niko instances handle data. It does not describe every copy of the software, because we do not run them.
- **Official public instances** (the bot invited from our website, and everything at niko.sryze.cc). All user data for these instances — account and server settings, economy and leveling records, AI memory, moderation and safety records, payment references, staff mail, and the anonymous usage counters — is stored in a **private MongoDB database** that we control. That database is not publicly reachable, is not shared with other bots or services, and is readable only with credentials held by the maintainers who operate Niko.
- **Private, beta, and self-hosted instances.** Niko's source is public, so anyone can run their own copy. Those deployments may use the **deprecated SQLite storage method** instead of MongoDB, may store data in JSON files or a different database, and may keep it on hardware we have never seen.
- **Self-hosted instances are outside our control.** We do not operate, host, administer, or have access to them, and we cannot read, export, correct, or delete anything they hold. We therefore **cannot handle data-removal requests, access requests, safety reports, or support requests about self-hosted, private, or beta instances**. Whoever runs such an instance is a separate controller: they decide what is collected, how long it is kept, how it is secured, and who can see it, and they are responsible for answering your requests and for their own legal obligations. Send any request about one of those instances to its operator, not to us.
- **How to tell which one you are using.** If the bot's profile, help command, or website links to niko.sryze.cc, you are on an official instance. If it points somewhere else, or was started by someone you know, treat its operator as the responsible party.
s2.title: Information we collect
s2.body:
We keep the categories below. Nothing else is collected for advertising, profiling, or resale.
- **Discord identifiers.** Your user ID links your economy balance, XP and level, reminders, birthday, highlights, AI memory, roleplay blocks, AFK state, and warnings to you. Server and channel IDs keep each server's settings apart from every other server's.
- **Message content.** Messages are read in real time to answer AI mentions, run automod and the scam filter, serve snipe and highlight commands, and award XP. Content is not stored as a chat log: it is stored only in the narrow cases listed in the retention schedule below (AI memory, the snipe cache, ticket transcripts, and reported scam images).
- **Names and avatars you already show in Discord.** Where a feature has to display a person — public leaderboards, staff profiles, server ownership records, ticket transcripts, giveaways, suggestions, and polls — the username, display name, and avatar URL are stored next to the record.
- **Server data.** Server name, icon URL, owner ID, member count, and the per-server configuration for every feature an admin has touched.
- **Content you submit.** Ticket transcripts, staff and team applications, appeals, reports, suggestions, polls, giveaways, birthdays, reminders, music playlists, and liked songs.
- **Presence, voice state, and activity.** Presence and voice state are read while a feature needs them (member lists, music, VoiceMaster) and are not stored. Daily message, join, and leave totals are stored as aggregate counters for the dashboard, without message text and without member IDs.
- **Scam-image reports.** When a member reports a message through the right-click scam report, the reported images and message context go to Niko staff for review. On confirmation, a perceptual hash (a compact numeric fingerprint) and a copy of the image are stored so variants can be detected and removed automatically.
- **Premium image moderation.** On a server with an active premium subscription, the URL of each image attachment posted there is sent to fal.ai's NSFW model so it can be scored. Niko stores the verdict (confidence score, file name, and moderation action), never the image itself.
- **Payments.** Premium subscriptions and donations are processed by OxaPay. We store the order reference, the OxaPay payment reference, the Discord user and server the payment belongs to, the amount and currency, the chosen crypto asset, the deposit address shown at checkout, and the payment status and timestamps. Niko never receives or stores card numbers, bank details, wallet private keys, or seed phrases.
- **Staff mail.** Mail sent to a Niko address on our own domain, and our replies to it, are stored so the team can read and answer them from one mailbox.
- **Global analytics.** Anonymous aggregate counters only, described in their own section below.
s3.title: AI features and Groq
s3.body:
Niko's AI replies, image understanding, and voice-message transcription are provided through [Groq](https://groq.com), an AI inference provider. Groq is the AI provider used by the official Niko instances; it is not an advertiser, a data broker, or a partner in any commercial sense.
- **What is sent.** When a member asks Niko to answer, Niko sends Groq the message being answered, the member's Discord username, the server name and member count, up to three recent turns of that member's AI conversation in that server, a short memory note, up to three recent channel messages used as context, a short excerpt of the message being replied to, and — when the member attached them — up to three image URLs or a transcription of their voice message.
- **Default models.** Chat runs on `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, image understanding on `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`, and transcription on `whisper-large-v3-turbo`. These defaults are configurable by the instance operator through the `GROQ_*` environment variables, so a self-hosted copy may use different models.
- **What Groq does with it.** Groq processes the request and returns a reply. Its handling of that request is governed by its own privacy policy and terms, which you should read alongside this one: [groq.com/privacy-policy](https://groq.com/privacy-policy/). We do not control Groq's infrastructure, and we cannot delete data that Groq keeps under its own policy.
- **What we do with it.** We use the reply to answer in Discord and store only the short conversation memory described in the retention schedule. We do not use your messages to train models, we do not sell them, and we do not share them with any other AI provider.
- **How to avoid it.** AI features are per-server and can be turned off by an admin in the dashboard. A member can erase their own conversation memory at any time with `/clearhistory`, and can simply not mention the bot. With AI disabled, no message content is sent to Groq.
s4.title: How we use information
s4.body: Data is used to run the features a server has enabled, to keep communities safe (automod, scam detection, moderation cases, blacklist enforcement, appeals), to answer support and staff mail, to keep payment and accounting records accurate, to fix bugs, and to decide which commands, fixes, and translations to work on next. We do not profile members for advertising, we do not build advertising audiences, and we do not sell, rent, or trade personal data to anyone.
s5.title: Legal bases, where the GDPR applies
s5.body: Where European data-protection law applies, we rely on: performance of a contract or your request (running the features a server enabled, answering your support mail); our legitimate interests (keeping communities safe from scams and abuse, preventing fraud, securing the service, and improving it with anonymous counters); compliance with legal obligations (accounting, tax, and responding to valid legal process); and consent where a feature asks for it. You may object to processing based on legitimate interests at any time through the data removal page or the support server, and we will stop unless we have an overriding legal ground — which, for preserved safety records, is usually the protection of other users.
s6.title: Storage and security
s6.body:
On official public instances, all user data is held in a private MongoDB database that we operate. Some auxiliary stores (for example the music library's playlists) live in a separate database on the same private infrastructure.
- Access is limited to the maintainers who run Niko, through credentials that are not published and are rotated when someone leaves the team. Staff members see only the parts of the dashboard their role allows.
- Traffic between Niko, Discord, our database, and the providers listed below is encrypted in transit.
- Payment card data never reaches us; OxaPay handles the checkout, and we store references rather than credentials.
- Where the database operator takes backups, they serve disaster recovery only, are access-restricted in the same way as the live database, and are rotated; deleted data ages out of them as they rotate.
- No system is perfectly secure. If a breach affects your data, we will announce it in the support server and, where the law requires it, notify the people affected and the relevant authority.
s7.title: Data retention policy
s7.body:
Retention is deliberate, not incidental. Each category below has a stated lifetime and a stated trigger. Where a fixed period is possible we use one; where a record exists to protect other people, we keep it for as long as that protection may be needed and say so plainly rather than promising a number we would not honour. Deletion, when it happens, removes the row from the live database immediately; a copy that sits inside a rotating backup ages out as that backup is replaced.
## How long we keep what
- **Economy, leveling, and profile data** (balances, XP, jobs, inventories, achievements, streaks, leaderboard privacy) — kept until you delete your account data through the data removal page, at which point the rows are removed.
- **Server configuration** (automod, logging, tickets, starboard, leveling, welcome, suggestions, notifier, and every other per-server setting) — kept while the server uses Niko, and removed when its owner completes a server deletion request.
- **AI conversation memory** — a rolling window of your last three exchanges per server plus a short memory note of a few hundred characters. It is overwritten continuously as you keep talking, so nothing older survives a new exchange. It is erased immediately by `/clearhistory`, by an account deletion, or by a server deletion.
- **Snipe cache** (the last deleted or edited message per channel) — held in memory only, overwritten by the next deletion in that channel, and cleared on every restart. Never written to disk.
- **Dashboard activity counters** (daily messages, joins, and leaves per server) — aggregate numbers only, with no message text and no member IDs; kept while the server uses Niko and removed with a server deletion.
- **Global analytics** — daily counters for the last 90 days plus lifetime totals, described in their own section below.
- **Logging revert snapshots** (the message state behind a “revert” button on a log entry) — pruned automatically after 30 days, on a sweep that runs at most once an hour.
- **Verification challenges** — minutes. A challenge is deleted as soon as it is solved, and expired challenges are swept automatically.
- **Temporary blacklists and timeouts** — deleted automatically the moment they expire; expiry is checked when the restriction is read and again on startup.
- **Permanent blacklists, warnings, mutes, moderation cases, giveaway bans, abuse strikes, ticket transcripts, and logging records** — kept without an automatic expiry for as long as they are needed to protect communities, settle appeals, and recognise repeat abuse. They survive account and server deletion requests, and are released only through the formal legal process described below.
- **Scam-image reports and confirmed fingerprints** — the report, the confirmed perceptual hash, and the stored image copy are kept while they remain useful for detecting variants, with no automatic expiry, because an expiring fingerprint would let known scam images return.
- **Premium image moderation verdicts** — kept with the server's premium records (score, file name, and action; never the image) for as long as the subscription record exists.
- **Payment and billing records** — Payment records are kept after a subscription ends, for accounting, tax, fraud prevention, refunds, chargeback windows, and billing support — typically for as long as accounting and tax law and the payment provider's dispute windows require. When that period ends, the record is deleted or reduced to figures that no longer identify you.
- **Data removal requests** — kept after completion as a compliance audit record: what was requested, what was removed, what was preserved, when, and by whom it was reviewed. This is how we can show that a deletion actually happened and that a preserved safety record was not erased.
- **Staff and team applications** — kept while an application is reviewed and afterwards as a recruitment record; removed with an account deletion request.
- **Birthdays, AFK state, reminders, roleplay blocks, giveaway entries, poll votes, and music playlists or liked songs** — kept until you remove them, the feature ends, or you delete your account data.
- **Server ownership records** (server ID, owner ID, name, icon, and whether Niko is still present) — kept after Niko is removed from a server so that its owner can still prove ownership and request deletion; it holds no member content.
- **Staff mail** — mail to a Niko address and our replies are kept so the conversation can be answered, audited, and handed over between staff roles; they are deleted when they are no longer needed for that purpose.
- **Aggregated and anonymised data** — totals and counters that cannot be traced back to a person or a server have no retention limit, because they are no longer personal data.
## What ends retention early
A completed account deletion request removes the personal and configuration data listed on the [data removal page](/data-removal); a completed server request does the same for a server you own. `/clearhistory` erases your AI memory immediately. Turning off a feature stops new collection at once. A restart clears the snipe cache. Expiry dates delete temporary restrictions without anyone asking.
## What survives a deletion request, and why
Moderation and safety records survive on purpose. They are the evidence that protects other communities: bot-level blacklists, warnings, mutes, moderation cases, logs and ticket transcripts, giveaway bans, abuse strikes, and scam-image reports. A deletion request never lifts a restriction, restores access, or erases evidence of abuse, and using one to try is a violation of the Terms of Service. Data removal requests themselves are kept as the audit trail described above.
## Legal holds and disputes
If a record is needed for an active investigation, an appeal, a payment dispute, a chargeback, or actual or threatened legal proceedings, its retention is extended until the matter is closed — including records that would otherwise have expired. Once the hold ends, the normal schedule applies again.
## Instances we do not run
This schedule describes official public instances only. Private, beta, and self-hosted deployments — including those still using the deprecated SQLite storage — set their own retention, and we cannot shorten, extend, enforce, or answer questions about it. Ask the operator of that instance.
s8.title: Your rights
s8.body:
Subject to the preserved records described above, and to the law where you live, you can ask to:
- **See** what Niko holds about you, and receive a copy of it.
- **Correct** anything wrong — most profile and settings fields you can change yourself in Discord or the dashboard.
- **Delete** your account data or a server you own through the data removal form.
- **Restrict or object** to a particular use, such as having your identity shown on the public leaderboard, which has its own privacy toggle in the dashboard.
- **Withdraw consent** for any feature that asked for it, by turning the feature off.
- **Complain** to your local data-protection authority. We would rather you came to us first, but you do not need our permission.
Every request is answered through the support server or the contact routes below, and we may ask you to prove control of the Discord account or server concerned so that nobody can delete somebody else's data.
s9.title: Data removal requests
s9.body:
You can request deletion of personal account data or of a server's configuration data through the [data removal form](/data-removal). You must sign in with Discord so ownership can be confirmed, and a server request remains available after Niko is removed if you were its owner at the time.
Every request is reviewed before deletion runs, so that a request cannot be used to erase a safety record or to escape a restriction. The review looks at the scope you asked for, your ownership evidence, and whether a legal hold applies. Requests are retained as a compliance audit record.
s10.title: Formal legal requests
s10.body: If a law requires deletion or release of a preserved safety record, send a formal request by email to the bot owner at [owner@niko.sryze.cc](mailto:owner@niko.sryze.cc). It must include a court record or signed legal document and the contact details of an official legal representative so authenticity can be verified. These matters are handled personally and confidentially; ordinary requests never override this process.
s11.title: Global analytics
s11.body: Niko keeps bot-wide usage statistics so that updates can be aimed at what communities actually use. What is counted is a daily total per command name, how each command was invoked (slash command, prefix command, or right-click/context command), the Discord language each server is set to, how many distinct servers used Niko that day, and the daily total of servers and members Niko is in. These are anonymous aggregate counters only: no message content, no user ID, no server or channel ID, and no individual person's activity is recorded, and a counter can never be traced back to a server or a person. The counters are kept for the last 90 days plus all-time totals, are visible only to Niko's staff, and are used solely to decide which features, fixes, and language translations to build and release next. Global analytics data is anonymous and is never seen, published, shared, or sold to any third-party company or individual.
s12.title: Third-party services
s12.body:
We share the minimum a feature needs, and only with the provider that feature uses:
- **Groq** — AI replies, image understanding, and voice transcription (see the AI section above), under [Groq's privacy policy](https://groq.com/privacy-policy/).
- **fal.ai** — premium image moderation, which sends image URLs for scoring, under [fal.ai's privacy policy](https://fal.ai/privacy). Never used on servers without premium.
- **OxaPay** — premium and donation payments, under [OxaPay's privacy policy](https://oxapay.com/privacy).
- **Discord** — everything Niko does happens on Discord and is subject to Discord's own privacy policy.
- **Hosting and infrastructure providers** — the servers and database where the official instances run.
- **Google Translate** — only when a translation feature is used, and only the text being translated.
Niko does not sell or rent personal data, does not use it for advertising, and does not share it with data brokers.
s13.title: Children
s13.body: Niko is not directed at children. Discord requires users to be at least 13 years old, or older where local law sets a higher minimum, and Niko follows that rule. If we learn that a child below the applicable age has used an official instance, we will remove their data on request from a parent or guardian and may restrict the account's access to Niko.
s14.title: International transfers
s14.body: Niko's maintainers and providers may process data in countries other than yours, including the United States. Where a transfer needs a legal safeguard, we rely on the provider's contractual protections and on the necessity of the transfer to deliver a feature you or your server asked for.
s15.title: Changes to this policy
s15.body:
Material changes — a new provider, a new category of data, or a shorter or longer retention period — are announced in the [support server](/discord) before or when they take effect, and the effective date at the top of this page moves. Continued use of Niko after a change constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.
Questions about this policy, a request under it, or a concern about how an official instance handled your data can be sent through the [support server](/discord).
